successors.note: Umar Tall took Nyamina on 25 May 1860, beat the Bambara army at Witala in September 1860 and entered Ségou on 10 March 1861. No dossier exists yet for the Tukulor Empire (group af-03-x).

capitals.name: Ségou
capitals.note: Coulibaly 'used the city as a capital for his new Bambara Empire'. The Bamana page's ruler list names Segou-Koro under Danfassari, an earlier seat that the page does not date.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1713 shape unchanged, applied for 1712-1747

keyframe_review.note: 23k km2 for 1713-1747, the Ségou and Mopti heartland: the Biton page has the empire founded in what is now Mali's Ségou and Mopti Regions, and the Bamana page dates the state from 1712 ('existed as a centralized state from 1712'). Shape unchanged; holds 1712-1747. The pages give no area, so there is no infobox figure to compare.

35k km2 for 1748-1751: the core plus a northern reach to 16.6 N. Fits the Biton page: Coulibaly 'attacked Tomboctou, though he held the city only briefly' (no year); the reach is read as that brief hold.
23k km2 for 1752-1756: the core again, Timbuktu given up. The Bamana page has Biton conquering Niani in 1751 and reigning to 1755.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1752 shape (the Ségou-Mopti core) repeated for 1757-1768

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1757-1768: Cliopatria has no Bamana shape for these twelve years, but the state lived on: Dinkoro and Ali reigned 1755-1766 in 'civil war and short reigns', and Ngolo Diarra 'seized the throne in 1766'. The 1752 core is repeated; the pages give no territorial change.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1769 core plus Timbuktu, for 1769-1799

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 23k km2 core for 1769-1799 lacks Timbuktu, but the Ngolo Diarra page says he 'defeated the Macina Empire and re-established firm control over Djenne and Timbuktu' (no year, within 1766-1790). Djenné and Massina lie in the core; a 100 km disc at Timbuktu is added.

35k km2 for 1800-1802: the core with the northern reach to Timbuktu, the same outline as 1748. Mansong Diarra (c. 1790-1808) 'earned renown as a great warrior, with defeats against several other groups, including Kaarta, Massina, Dogon, and Mossi'; no campaign is dated.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1803 shape unchanged, applied for 1803-1817

keyframe_review.note: 104,716 km2 (3.7 to 6.3 W up to 2.5 W, 13 to 16.7 N) for 1803-1819: Ségou, Massina, the Niger bend and the Dogon plateau. The Mansong page names Massina and the Dogon among his defeated groups (undated). The Bamana page has Da Diarra (1808-1827) 'lost control of Macina' and the Battle of Noukouma in 1818, so the shape holds 1803-1817. Same outline Cliopatria later gives the Massina Empire (1822-1860).

correction.text: Ségou and its surroundings: the part of the empire left after Noukouma (the pages give no extent)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1818-1861: what is left after Massina breaks away. 'At the Battle of Noukouma in 1818, Bambara forces met and were defeated by Fula Muslim fighters'; the Massina forces then took Djenné and much of the territory around Mopti. Segou stood until 10 March 1861. The pages give no extent for these decades, so a 100 km disc around Ségou is used (confidence 1 on the area). Cliopatria ends the Bamana row in 1821 and later draws this land as Massina.

correction.text: Ségou and its surroundings: the part of the empire left after Noukouma (the pages give no extent)

keyframe_review.note: 12k km2 speck at 3.9-2.6 W, 16.0-16.7 N, around Timbuktu, for 1820-1821. No page puts the Bamana at Timbuktu after Noukouma; the Massina page has Seku Amadu 'in 1826/7 conquered Timbuktu'. The Bamana state in these years is the Ségou remnant (bamana-empire_1818).

ledger.note: 1712: Mamari (Biton) Coulibaly founds the Bambara state at Ségou. He became leader in 1712 after being elected head of the tòn; 'existed as a centralized state from 1712'. The Biton page's tomb inscription reads 'Reign 1712-1755'; the Kaladian line before him is dated 'Around 1640'.
Undated, under Biton Coulibaly (1712-1755): he 'attacked Tomboctou, though he held the city only briefly.' 1748 is Cliopatria's step; the page gives no year (page silent).

1751: the Mansa of Mali becomes a vassal. The page says that in 1751 Biton conquered Niani, making the Mali Empire's Mansa a vassal. The mali-empire dossier ends the empire c. 1610 (Manden remnant), so the pages disagree about whether a Mansa existed in 1751.
Undated: Biton 'held the city only briefly', so Timbuktu is given up by Cliopatria's 1752 shape (page silent on the year).
1766: Ngolo Diarra seizes the throne from the Coulibaly line. 'Ngolo Diarra, by now a leader of the ton djon, seized the throne in 1766 and soon restored order.' Same state, same colour (rule 2).

Between 1766 and 1790: Ngolo Diarra 'defeated the Macina Empire and re-established firm control over Djenne and Timbuktu.' The page gives no year; 1769 is the start of Cliopatria's Diarra shape (page silent). Only Timbuktu is added, since Djenné and Massina lie inside the core.

wars.name: Biton Coulibaly's wars
wars.outcome: Conquests of the Fulani, Soninke, Mossi and of Macina, Beledougou, Djenné, Bamako (undated); a Kong invasion beaten in 1725; Timbuktu attacked and held only briefly; the Mansa of Mali made a vassal after Niani in 1751.

wars.name: Ségou succession wars
wars.outcome: 'Civil war and short reigns' under Dinkoro and Ali until Ngolo Diarra seized the throne in 1766; no land recorded as changing hands.

wars.outcome: Ngolo 'defeated the Macina Empire and re-established firm control over Djenne and Timbuktu' (undated); he died in a campaign against the Mossi in 1790 (the Park passage implies 1795).

notes: Pages opened: five (budget 5); the Massina page serves this dossier and massina-empire. Every page is thin on dates: no conquest under Biton, Ngolo or Mansong is dated, so each Cliopatria step (1748, 1752, 1769, 1800, 1803) is a confidence-1 bridge; no page gives an area (no infobox comparison possible). Cliopatria's Bamana row stops in 1821 and relabels the 104,716 km2 outline as Massina (1822-1860), yet the Bamana page runs the state to 10 March 1861; the dossier adds a 1818-1861 Ségou remnant (a 100 km disc, extent not on any page) and marks the Timbuktu speck of 1820-21 wrong. The massina-empire dossier removes this remnant from its shape. The 1751 vassalage of the Mansa of Mali rests on one sentence and sits badly with the mali-empire dossier (empire ended c. 1610). Dates disagree inside the Bamana page: Kaladian c. 1640 or 1652-1672, Ngolo 1766-1787 (list) or 1790 (text and Ngolo page; the Park passage implies 1795), Mansong c. 1790 or 1788-1808. No rulers strip: the list on the page is incomplete and inconsistent. Not mapped: the Kong invasion of 1725 (no land), Kaarta, Bélédougou, Bamako, the Mossi and Dogon frontiers. Counterparts needing dossiers: tukulor-empire, pashalik-of-timbuktu (saadi-sultanate dossier uses the slug), Kong, Kaarta, Ardo of Massina. Gazetteer lacks Nyamina, Witala, Niani, Macina (the Dogon plateau is not a named region).
